title: AI-guided CDR-H3 design with phage display yields TIGIT-binding antibodies
summary: The SANDAN workflow used DiffAb diffusion-based CDR-H3 design on templates predicted by Boltz-1, with no known binding antibody supplied as input. A phage library of about 1,000 designed CDR-H3 sequences yielded six human TIGIT-binding antibodies that compete with the reference antibody MG1131 and carry distinct CDR-H3 sequences. Binding affinities are not given in the abstract.
ai_technology: DiffAb diffusion design on Boltz-1 predicted structures (SANDAN workflow)
organization: Institute of Science Tokyo; Astellas Pharma

evidence.tested: Phage display screening and competition assays of about 1,000 designed CDR-H3 sequences against human TIGIT.
evidence.unknown: Binding affinities and function not stated in the abstract; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Diffusion-based model designing CDR-H3 loops on predicted complex structures.
